Observed_SHAP_Pattern (Association): Uncontrolled crossings and Y/X-shaped junctions create high-angle conflict points.
Pre_Crash_Prevention (Prevent Event): Convert high-severity X/Y crossings into roundabouts, channelized turns, or signalized junctions.
Crash_Phase_Protection (Reduce Injury): Raised junction tables and speed humps that physically lower impact speeds at intersections.
Post_Crash_Care (Save Lives): Clear junction location signage to speed up emergency caller location reporting.

Observed_SHAP_Pattern (Association): Saturday and Sunday crashes show higher severe/fatal rates due to lighter traffic, higher speeds, and social travel.
Pre_Crash_Prevention (Prevent Event): Targeted weekend speed & sobriety checkpoints (FRSC corridor patrols near markets, worship, and leisure zones).
Crash_Phase_Protection (Reduce Injury): Strict seat-belt, child-restraint, and motorcycle helmet enforcement on weekend trips.
Post_Crash_Care (Save Lives): Dedicated weekend trauma-team readiness and rapid ambulance dispatch along arterial routes.

Observed_SHAP_Pattern (Association): Weekend vs. weekday travel patterns shift speed, recreational travel, and enforcement coverage.
Pre_Crash_Prevention (Prevent Event): Weekend sobriety/speed checkpoints along recreational, market, and religious corridors.
Crash_Phase_Protection (Reduce Injury): Consistent occupant restraint enforcement across weekend travel peaks.
Post_Crash_Care (Save Lives): Weekend trauma-center staffing aligned with Friday–Sunday crash patterns.

Observed_SHAP_Pattern (Association): Single-vehicle & pedestrian impacts carry much higher severe/fatal rates than multi-vehicle urban queues.
Pre_Crash_Prevention (Prevent Event): Segregated pedestrian walkways, speed calming in mixed-traffic zones, and roadside hazard removal.
Crash_Phase_Protection (Reduce Injury): Forgiving roadside barriers, pedestrian-friendly vehicle fronts, and median guardrails.
Post_Crash_Care (Save Lives): Rapid emergency dispatch protocols along high-speed single-vehicle rollover/pedestrian corridors.

Observed_SHAP_Pattern (Association): Night-time vs. daytime traffic periods shift collision speed and visibility risk profiles.
Pre_Crash_Prevention (Prevent Event): Staggered commercial haulage scheduling and dusk-to-dawn speed management.
Crash_Phase_Protection (Reduce Injury): Conspicuity retro-reflective tape on heavy trucks and buses operating after dusk.
Post_Crash_Care (Save Lives): Off-peak emergency hotline prioritization along inter-urban/arterial corridors.

Observed_SHAP_Pattern (Association): Late-night and early-morning hours show elevated fatal/serious risk despite lower traffic volume.
Pre_Crash_Prevention (Prevent Event): Targeted night-time speed & alcohol/fatigue enforcement patrols (FRSC night corridor operations).
Crash_Phase_Protection (Reduce Injury): High-visibility reflective road markings and mandatory seat-belt/helmet compliance at night.
Post_Crash_Care (Save Lives): 24-hour trauma response readiness and dedicated night-shift ambulance staging.

Observed_SHAP_Pattern (Association): Younger and unrecorded-age drivers show elevated involvement in severe crash configurations.
Pre_Crash_Prevention (Prevent Event): Graduated driver licensing, stricter probation rules, and targeted youth road-safety education.
Crash_Phase_Protection (Reduce Injury): Mandatory seat-belt and helmet enforcement across young commercial and private riders.
Post_Crash_Care (Save Lives): Emergency medical linkage via standardized driver licence registry data.

Observed_SHAP_Pattern (Association): Unsafe overtaking, lane-changing, speeding, and failure to give way elevate crash severity.
Pre_Crash_Prevention (Prevent Event): Automated speed cameras, lane-discipline enforcement, and defensive driver licensing audits.
Crash_Phase_Protection (Reduce Injury): Speed-limiting devices (already mandated for commercial fleets by FRSC) to cap kinetic energy.
Post_Crash_Care (Save Lives): Post-crash blackspot review linking police crash-cause logs to road redesign.

Observed_SHAP_Pattern (Association): Undivided two-way carriageways expose opposing traffic to severe head-on and overtaking crashes.
Pre_Crash_Prevention (Prevent Event): Install physical median barriers or rumble strips on undivided multi-lane corridors.
Crash_Phase_Protection (Reduce Injury): Energy-absorbing median guardrails that prevent cross-median intrusions.
Post_Crash_Care (Save Lives): Emergency turnaround access gates planned safely into divided medians.
